title: MAYDAY: rough engine over the pines

briefing.airport: En route near Cedar Valley — with Big Sky Approach
briefing.description: You're cruising with flight following when the engine starts running rough and the oil pressure needle sags. Time to use the radio the way it was ultimately designed to be used. The distress call is MAYDAY three times, then who you are, what's wrong, where you are, and what you want. Expect ATC to ask for souls on board and fuel remaining — it's routine, answer calmly.

steps.text: Level at 4,500, 15 miles west of Centerville, the engine coughs. RPM drops, the airframe shudders, oil pressure is falling. Carb heat on, mixture rich — still rough. You're already talking to Big Sky Approach. Declare.

steps.prompt: Declare the emergency: MAYDAY three times, who you are, the problem, your position and altitude, and what you want (vectors to the nearest airport).
steps.hint: Mayday mayday mayday, Skyhawk {callsign}, rough running engine, one five miles west of Centerville at four thousand five hundred, request vectors to the nearest airport.

elements.label: MAYDAY three times
elements.feedbackMissing: Open with “MAYDAY, MAYDAY, MAYDAY” — three times is the standard, and it instantly clears the frequency for you.

elements.label: your callsign
elements.feedbackMissing: Say who you are — rescuers can't help an anonymous airplane.

elements.label: your position
elements.feedbackMissing: Give your position — “one five miles west of Centerville”. It's the single most important piece if the engine quits entirely.

elements.label: your altitude
elements.feedbackMissing: Include your altitude — it tells ATC how much glide time you have.
elements.feedbackWrong: You said {heard} feet, but you're at 4,500.

elements.label: what you want
elements.feedbackMissing: Tell them what you need: “request vectors to the nearest airport”.

steps.speaker: Approach
steps.text: Skyhawk {callsign}, roger mayday. Nearest airport is Cedar Valley, one zero miles south of your position. Turn right heading one niner zero. Say souls on board and fuel remaining.

steps.prompt: Read back the heading and answer: two people aboard, three hours of fuel.
steps.hint: Heading one niner zero, two souls on board, three hours fuel, Skyhawk {callsign}.

elements.label: heading readback
elements.feedbackMissing: Read back the heading: “heading one niner zero” — it's your lifeline to the field.

elements.label: souls on board
elements.feedbackMissing: Answer the question: “two souls on board”.

elements.label: fuel remaining
elements.feedbackMissing: Answer the fuel question: “three hours fuel”.

elements.label: your callsign
elements.feedbackMissing: In an emergency, brevity wins — but a callsign still helps when you have the breath for it.

steps.speaker: Approach
steps.text: Skyhawk {callsign}, Cedar Valley is twelve o'clock, eight miles. Equipment is standing by. Descend at your discretion — runway one eight is the favored runway, winds one seven zero at six.
The engine is still making partial power. There — the runway, dead ahead through the haze.

steps.prompt: Tell Approach you have the field in sight.

elements.label: field in sight
elements.feedbackMissing: Report “field in sight” — it tells ATC you can complete the approach visually.

steps.speaker: Approach
steps.text: Skyhawk {callsign}, roger. Cleared to proceed direct Cedar Valley, change to advisory frequency approved. Good luck — we'll be watching until you're down.

steps.prompt: Acknowledge and switch — you'll self-announce at Cedar Valley from here.
steps.hint: Direct Cedar Valley, over to advisory, Skyhawk {callsign}. Thanks for the help.

steps.text: You glide it in and roll out safely at Cedar Valley. Remember: declaring an emergency costs nothing — no paperwork for asking for help, and every resource in the system turns toward you the moment you say MAYDAY.
